correctness.rationale: For every connected H of order at least three, an independent set in C(H) contains a clique X of original vertices plus subdivision vertices corresponding only to edges of H-X; connectedness gives at least |X| edges incident with X, so alpha(C(H))=|E(H)|. Substituting this identity and the exact order-size formulas for a central graph into Theorem 2.12 of arXiv:2609.16357v1 simplifies exactly to i(C^k(G))=2|E(C^(k-2)(G))| for k>=3, with K2,k=3 checked separately through P3.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The September 2026 source gives the exact second-iterate formula but does not state higher iterates. Searches for exact and synonymous higher-iterate formulations found no prior theorem implying the all-k identity. The elementary alpha(C(H)) lemma may be known separately, so the originality claim is centered on the higher-iterate independent-domination identity and its consequences.

value.rationale: The theorem determines every central iterate from the third onward and shows that all finer graph structure disappears from these values: the entire tail depends only on the starting order and size through a deterministic recurrence.
